extracted.intended_audience: eligible hospitals and critical access hospitals (CAHs), health IT vendors, and other stakeholders responding to CMS notice-and-comment on the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed rule provisions and criteria for measures, reporting, exclusions, scoring, and related requests for information under the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program (applicable to eligible hospitals and CAHs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Prior Authorization measure (initial reporting and scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: When we adopted the Electronic Prior Authorization measure in the 2024 Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule, we finalized that eligible hospitals and CAHs would report the measure as an unscored attestation for only the EHR reporting period in CY 2027, but we did not specify its scoring methodology for subsequent years because we determined that it would be more appropriate to determine the measure's scoring structure closer in time to its effective date. In this proposed rule, we are also proposing that the Electronic Prior Authorization measure would remain unscored for the EHR reporting period in CY 2028 and subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting format: unscored attestation for CY2027 and proposed unscored for CY2028 and subsequent years (initial approach to allow adjustment to workflow without scoring focus). CMS invites public comment on the proposal and on possible future updates to incentivize broader use. The measure is seen as important to health information exchange and meaningful use. CMS also proposes the option of making the measure an optional bonus measure for the EHR reporting period in CY 2027. Comments are specifically invited on how to strengthen the measure while minimizing burden and on barriers small, rural, or under-resourced hospitals and CAHs might face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Prior Authorization measure exclusions (as adopted in 2024 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The available exclusions would be: (1) an eligible hospital or CAH did not order any medical item or services (excluding drugs) requiring prior authorization during the EHR reporting period; or (2) the eligible hospital or CAH only ordered medical items or services (excluding drugs) requiring prior authorization from a payer that does not offer an API that meets CMS's specified Prior Authorization API requirements during the applicable EHR reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exclusions (originally adopted in the 2024 Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule) would be available to eligible hospitals and CAHs for the EHR reporting period in CY 2028 and subsequent years. Comment sought on any additional exclusions that should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for information: design considerations for a future performance-based Electronic Prior Authorization measure
rubrics_metrics.description: While the current requirement of achieving 'at least one' electronic prior authorization is appropriate for initial inclusion, CMS does not expect this minimal requirement to effectively increase electronic prior authorization usage over time and is seeking comments on potential future updates to incentivize more substantial use during an EHR reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests input on: how to expand the scope to increase interoperable data exchange and reduce administrative burden; ways to drive consistent adoption of certified health IT supporting the complete electronic prior authorization workflow; how to incentivize addressing a wider array of prior authorization requests that require complex payer interactions; and barriers faced by small/rural/under-resourced hospitals. Public input will inform future considerations and potential performance-based measure design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Device Identifiers (UDI) for Implantable Medical Devices measure — measure description
rubrics_metrics.description: The eligible hospital or CAH uses CEHRT during the EHR reporting period to electronically capture and store, as one or more discrete data elements within the patient's electronic health record, the complete Unique Device Identifier (UDI), which includes the device identifier and, when present on the device label, the production identifier, for each implantable medical device subject to UDI requirements used for patient care delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reporting: 'Yes' or 'No' attestation. This measure is proposed to be required beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2027 and would be one of seven measures required to satisfy the Public Health and Clinical Data Exchange objective. No points will be assigned to this measure initially; both 'Yes' and 'No' responses would be allowed to fulfill initial measure requirements to allow familiarization while avoiding undue burden. CMS invites comments on feasibility, timeline, and additional exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: UDI measure exclusions and scope (applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion: The eligible hospital or CAH implanted five or fewer medical devices subject to UDI requirements during the calendar year of the applicable EHR reporting period. The measure only applies to implantable medical devices subject to UDI requirements under 21 CFR 801.20(a) and 21 CFR part 830, subpart E; some devices (investigational devices, devices for research use only, and custom devices) are exempt from UDI requirements and therefore exempt from this measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS invites comments on any additional exclusions. The proposal references device labeling and GUDID as the statutory/technical basis for UDI, and notes that UDI data elements are present in US Core Data for Interoperability Version 3 and supported via FHIR. If relevant ONC certification criteria are removed in separate rulemaking, CMS would reconsider referenced certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for information: design considerations for a future performance-based UDI measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Should CMS adopt the measure, they intend to consider future modifications and invite public comment on questions related to a performance-based measure to assess meaningful use of UDI data (for example, numerator/denominator design and data sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific questions CMS seeks comment on include: how to define an appropriate denominator (all implantable devices, procedure codes, device categories); categories of devices challenging for capture; measures to ensure UDI data quality and whether CEHRT should validate UDI accuracy/format against GUDID; challenges when multiple devices are used in an episode; whether to assess making UDI available for exchange via certified health IT (eg, FHIR API); requiring UDI in discharge/after-visit summaries or patient portals; measures showing UDI used for quality comparison, recalls, follow-up care; whether to set performance thresholds with numerator/denominator and phased-in thresholds; applicability to other care settings and technical/workflow barriers (barcode scanning infrastructure, EHR limitations); and existing workflows/technologies (automated scanning, supply chain integration) that could reduce burden while maintaining data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring methodology for the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program (performance-based scoring and point structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: In FY 2019 CMS adopted a performance-based scoring methodology for eligible hospitals and CAHs, including a minimum scoring threshold. For EHR reporting period in CY 2027, the points associated with required measures sum to 100 points and reporting on optional bonus measures offers up to an additional 15 bonus points (total up to 115). For CY 2028 and subsequent years, required measures sum to 100 points, with a total possible score up to 105 (Electronic Prior Authorization proposed as a required measure in CY 2028; 5 bonus points remain available under the Public Health and Clinical Data Exchange objective). CMS previously finalized increases to the minimum scoring threshold to 70 points for CY 2025 and 80 points for CY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores for required and bonus measures are added to calculate total score. The maximum points listed for measures do not include points redistributed if an exclusion is claimed. CMS is not proposing changes to point redistribution policy; readers are referred to tables showing point redistribution for CY2027 and CY2028. CMS codified a measure suppression policy (§495.24(f)(3)) enabling suppression (exclusion) of a measure from assessment if certain circumstances impact performance assessment — in such cases, CMS would allocate maximum points or provide full credit if the affected measure is reported, or exclude the affected measure from meaningful EHR user determination if the measure is not scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM reporting requirement and alignment with Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sections 1814(l)(3)(A) and 1886(n)(3)(A) of the Act and the definition of 'meaningful EHR user' under 42 CFR 495.4, eligible hospitals and CAHs must report on clinical quality measures (electronic clinical quality measures, or eCQMs) selected by CMS using CEHRT as part of the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program. Section 1886(n)(3)(B)(i)(I) of the Act requires the Secretary to provide preference for selection of clinical quality measures that are also used in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program or endorsed by the consensus-based entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS intends to continue aligning eCQM reporting requirements and measure sets for the Promoting Interoperability Program with the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program to improve coordination and reduce burden. Eligible hospitals and CAHs are currently required to annually report data for each required eCQM and three self-selected eCQMs for CY2026 and subsequent years; CMS proposes to modify these requirements beginning with the CY2028 reporting period to more closely align with Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and remove specific eCQM measures (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is proposing to adopt two eCQMs in the Promoting Interoperability Program eCQM measure set beginning with CY2028: (1) Hospital Harm—Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism; and (2) Advance Care Planning. CMS is proposing to remove three eCQMs beginning with CY2028: (1) Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy; (2) Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis eCQM; and (3) Intensive Care Unit Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS invites public comment on these proposals and refers readers to tables summarizing eCQMs available by reporting period and proposed policies to modify reporting and submission requirements beginning with CY2028.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed modification to eCQM reporting and submission timing (progression from self-selected to mandatory reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with alignment to the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program, CMS proposes that certain Hospital Harm eCQMs become mandatory for reporting after 2 years of self-selected reporting. Specifically: Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury and Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure would become mandatory beginning with CY2028 (after two years of self-selected reporting). The Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE eCQM would be available for self-selected reporting for CY2028 and CY2029 and would become mandatory beginning with CY2030, if finalized. CMS also proposes to require mandatory reporting of the Malnutrition Care Score eCQM beginning with CY2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These proposed changes are intended to incentivize improvements in patient safety and nutrition care. The referenced eCQMs would continue to be available as self-selected measures for the CY2027 reporting period. CMS invites public comment and refers readers to other sections for detailed rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEAM (Transforming Episode Accountability Model) episode definition and inclusion/cancellation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under TEAM, an episode has two significant dimensions: (1) a clinical dimension describing which clinical conditions and associated services are included; and (2) a time dimension describing when the episode begins and ends. TEAM episodes begin when a beneficiary is admitted for an anchor hospitalization or an anchor procedure identified by specific MS-DRGs or HCPCS codes (42 CFR 512.525(d)). Episodes include all non-excluded Medicare Parts A and B items and services during the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure and a 30-day post-discharge period (42 CFR 512.525(e)), with limited exclusions outlined in 42 CFR 512.525(f). An episode may be cancelled if the beneficiary does not meet inclusion criteria (42 CFR 512.535), dies during the anchor hospitalization or procedure, or the episode qualifies for the extreme and uncontrollable circumstances policy (42 CFR 512.537(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TEAM tests five surgical episode categories selected for high-expenditure, high-volume care and greater post-acute spending: CABG, LEJR, Major Bowel Procedure, SHFFT, and Spinal Fusion. CMS assesses MS-DRG classification changes annually and notes such changes may affect episode volume and beneficiary inclusion. CMS is proposing updates to the spinal fusion episode category to account for MS-DRG changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEAM participation structure and payment/quality incentives (tracks and glide path)
rubrics_metrics.description: All acute care hospitals, with limited exceptions, located within CMS-selected CBSAs for model implementation are required to participate in TEAM. CMS allowed a one-time voluntary opt-in for certain hospitals previously in BPCI Advanced or CJR not located in mandatory CBSAs. TEAM includes a 1-year glide path to ease participants into full financial risk and three participation tracks: Track 1 (upside-only, available to all participants in first performance year and to safety-net hospitals for first 3 years); Track 2 (two-sided, lower risk/reward than Track 3, available to select participants in performance years 2–5); Track 3 (two-sided, higher risk/reward, available to all participants performance years 1–5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes are assessed by comparing actual Medicare FFS spending to reconciliation target prices (based on baseline data, trend, discount, and risk-adjustment) and by selected quality measures. Participants may earn payments if spending is below target (subject to quality adjustment) or owe repayments if above target (subject to quality adjustment). CMS proposes modifications to TEAM including adding MS-DRGs to spinal fusion category, adjusting episode attribution, measurement periods, baseline construction, and capturing APC/MS-DRG changes in preliminary target prices.
